THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Research by economists at the Australian National University reveals that Australia's share of the markets of East Asia shrank from 4.05 per cent of imports in 1985 to 2.89 per cent in 1993 - the equivalent to about A$12 billion in exports. The figures indicate the importance of Prime Minister John Howard's trip to Japan and Indonesia this week to outline his agenda for reform of the Australian economy. Page 1.

Superannuation fund administrators would be able to calculate individual members' taxable income almost precisely under the Federal Government's new plan to impose a 15 per cent tax surcharge on superannuation contributions. The privacy breaches would ocurr because the assessments of the extra tax payable would be issued by the Australian Taxation Office to the superannuation funds, rather than to the individual taxpayer or member of the fund. Page 1.

Tasmanian Premier Tony Rundle has told the Federal Government his State should get more than three times as much from the A$1.15 billion Natural Heritage Trust as it would receive on a per capita basis and Independent Senator Brian Harradine has also expressed concern that the Commonwealth recognise Tasmania's natural heritage when setting up the environmental legislation. Harradine has threatened to vote against the Government's Telstra sale legislation if it does not consider raising revenue from the prvatisation through the issue of redeemable share options. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Contrary to Communications Minister Richard Alston's claim that there was "no windfall gain" arising from Telstra's huge A$2.3 billion profit, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer yesterday suggested that a couple of hundred million dollars could be spent on a constitutional convention on the republic next year. However, the Federal Opposition warned Prime Minister John Howard not to use abortion and family planning funding as a bargaining chip in negotiations with Independent Senator Brian Harradine over the proposed Telstra sale. Page 1.

Although Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer met Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama at the weekend, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said yesterday he had no plans to meet the man during his Australian visit. Prime Minister John Howard leaveson a six-day trip to Indonesia and Japan today, but he is expected to conduct a private meeting with the Dalai Lama when he returns next week. Page 1.

The Sydney Olympic logo has received mixed reactions from all parts of the community. Federal ALP president Barry Jones labelled the logo "a collection of cliches", while New South Wales Labor Premier Bob Carr approved of the design. However, the use of boomerangs in the logo has upset some Aboriginal activists, with Michael Mansell calling for Aborigines to boycott products carrying the logo and Charles Perkins expressing his annoyance at the Sydney Organising Committee's failure to consult Aborigines bfore using the boomerangs. Page 3.

In an effort to meet its Budget promise of cutting A$500 million in spending, the Queensland Government is considering shifting some Government welfare functions over to charities, contracting out hospital maintenance, catering, cleaning and laundry servies and contracting out more services in all Government departments. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A Reserve Bank study to be released today, The Future of the Financial System, reveals that banks will be forced to increase fees for basic services because of serious threat from cut-price specialists. The report concludes that banks will continue to exist even though technological change and new competition mean they are unlikely to remain as integrated conglomerates with big networks of branches. Page 1.

Despite an election promise to let the people select half the delegates for the People's Constitutional Convention on the republic next year, the Federal Government is now considering a plan to let the States appoint these delegates, with the remainder beng selected by the Commonwealth. Page 1.

A 50 per cent slump in annual funding for the Geneva-based World Council of Churches since 1991 has prompted the council to consider immediate cutbacks to staff and human rights and disaster relief programs. Linking 400 million Christians in 100 countries, the council is expecting only A$62 million in income
this year. Page 3.

According to the New South Wales Government, the Royal National Park, first legally gazetted in 1879, is the oldest national park in the world. Known as the second-oldest national park in the world behind the US's Yellowstone, the Government says The Royal was legally declared a national park four years earlier than Yellowstone. Page 3.
THE AGE

Several judges have accused Victorian Attorney-General Jan Wade of neglecting the traditional role of the Attorney-General, which was to defend the courts and the judiciary. The judges also criticised a State Government sentencing survey which found supprt for tougher sentences for a range of serious crimes. Page A1.

Using sophisticated mathematical techniques, a team of Australian and American scientists has proved for the first time a classical model of the cosmos demonstrating that the universe began and may end in chaos. Scientists in Melbourne and San
Francisco hve proved the case for a debate which has continued for more than 30 years amongst scientists around the world. Page A1.

Keen to obtain Independent Senator Brian Harradine's support for its proposed Telstra sale, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer yesterday confirmed that the Government might reconsider Medicare funding for abortions, an issue in which Harradine has an interest. Page A1.

Although it could risk provoking an angry response from China, Tibetan spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, has indicated he would like to meet with Prime Minister John Howard, following promising talks with Foreign Minister Alexander Downer over the prospec of brokering talks between China and Tibetan spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, has indicated he would like to meet with Prime Minister Alexander Downer over the prospect of brockering talks between China and Tibetan leaders on autonomy for the ancient Himalayan Kingdom. Page A3
